header.running_head: Admonition to Those Who Flee the Battlefield in the path of Allaah

blocks.text: He then fell to the ground. His two slaves bend over him saying:
"The slave protects his master as well as himself"
However, the enemy soon closed in on him and cut off his head.[^1]

Hadhrat Is'haaq bin Abi Is'haaq says, "I was present when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) was martyred in the Masjidul Haraam. The armies continued entering through the doors of the Masjid and each time one entered, he drove them back single-handedly. As he was doing this, one of the rocks of the Masjid fell on his head and floored him. He was then reciting the following couplet (which meant):

'O (beloved mother) Asmaa! Do not weep for me if I am killed
For my ancestry and Deen are still intact
So is my sword that my right hand is now too weak to hold'"[^2]
Admonition to Those Who Flee the Battlefield in the path of Allaah
The Sahabah (RA) Admonish Hadhrat Salama bin Hishaam (RA)

Hadhrat Ummu Salama (RA) once asked the wife of Hadhrat Salama bin Hishaam bin Mughiera (RA), "Why do I not see (your husband) Salama attend the salaah with Rasulullaah ﷺ and the Muslims?" She replied, "By Allaah! He is unable to leave the house because whenever he does so, people shout at him saying, 'Deserter! Did you flee in the path of Allaah?!' This reached the extent that he now sits at home and is unable to leave." He had participated in the Battle of Mu'ta with Hadhrat Khaalid bin Waleed (RA).[^3]
A Man Admonishes Hadhrat Abu Hurayra (RA)

Hadhrat Abu Hurayra (RA) says, "There was a problem between my cousin and myself. However, I had no reply to give him when he provoked me by saying, 'Were you not one of those who fled during the Battle of Mu'ta?'"[^4]
